name: Entity Graph
blurb: Every company, model, paper, person, dataset, benchmark, and regulation as a node.

nodes.scheme: DOI or arXiv id, linked to the original publisher
arXiv id from the model's own tags
registry id from the official MCP registry

reading.body:
Open models outnumber every other node category by an order of magnitude: 15,247 entries against 425 API models, 269 companies, and 64 tracked people, making the open model layer the largest single surface in this graph by a wide margin.

The regulatory layer is the second-largest mass in the graph, and it is almost entirely state-level. 3,013 state AI bills and 109 lawsuits together account for more tracked nodes than all companies, people, datasets, benchmarks, hardware entries, and repositories combined. That concentration reflects where legislative activity has accumulated, though the data records the existence of bills rather than their status or effect. The 67 compliance documents, keyed to ISO, NIST, and EU standards, are a much smaller set and cover a different kind of obligation entirely.

The parts of the graph most directly connected to compute and infrastructure are comparatively sparse. 37 hardware entries and 55 repositories sit alongside only 17 tracked datasets and 18 benchmarks. The hardware count is small enough that significant gaps are likely, and the data does not indicate which hardware generations or vendors are covered. What the graph does not yet contain matters as much as what it does: 1 tool entry and 17 datasets suggest those node types are early in collection rather than representative of their actual populations.
